Y Combinator flew me out to SF, and I just had the best weekend at Startup School. My main takeaways from Startup School: • Jensen Huang : approach every new problem with "how hard can it be?" • Sam Altman: get comfortable with people calling your idea dumb, or not liking it at all • Jeff Dean : thought experiments are one of the most underrated tools for building systems that matter • Garry Tan : be earnest I would like to thank fellow University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign alum & General Partner at YC, Pete Koomen , for extending the invite. I had cold-emailed him a while back, and that email turning into an invite for Startup School is something I am very grateful for. Beyond that, just getting to spend two days surrounded by builders from every kind of background, different countries, different industries, and different stages of their journey, was genuinely energizing. #ycstartupschool

Spoke last Friday on Distributed Training and Inference on Kubernetes with KubeRay at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) AI Technical Community Group. We walked through KubeRay as a platform for running distributed training, batch inference, and online serving on Kubernetes. Covered cluster lifecycle, accelerators, scheduling, observability, and what’s next for the project. Loved getting to speak about Ray/KubeRay/K8s from outside the usual OSS contributor lens. Thanks to Julio Perez and Josh Halley for the invite, to Nary Yeh and Jun-Hao Wan for presenting with me, and to opensource4you (ALC Taipei) for the opportunity.. Event: https://lnkd.in/g_We877P #KubeRay #Ray #Kubernetes #MLInfrastructure #DistributedSystems #DistributedTraining #Inference #GPU #CNCF #OpenSource

It's been a while... 😊 And a lot has changed... . . . I've never been a fan of LinkedIn accomplishment posts. Personally, they always felt incomplete, only showing the part that makes sense after everything worked out. This one's the opposite. Yes, I finished undergrad, my master's, switched jobs and cities. It looks like a straight line on paper. It wasn't one to live through. While I gained plenty, I lost some too. Some that weigh more than the rest combined...the kind where you can point to a single month on a calendar and know exactly what changed after it. One small example, I miss being a TA. The weekly ritual of labs, discussions, and office hours. Students came for advice on courses, interviews, sometimes even life. Not because I had answers...I just guessed a couple right ones and never corrected the record. Turns out I wasn't there just to teach statistics. Mostly, we were all just keeping confusion company, and I was the one billing it as office hours. I miss that. However, those kinds of deep conversations didn't disappear. It just lost its classroom. A few questions I've been sitting with lately: 1. Why do we tend to measure ourselves against people who might not be running the same race? 2. Why does anxiety of not being everywhere and/or doing everything creep up even when things are actually fine? 3. How do you lead yourself before trying to lead anyone else? In the coming weeks, I will be trying to spend some more time with these questions (one-by-one) and share some of my thoughts...and what I hope is some of y'all will chime in. Would love to recreate the classroom I had...virtually. 🙂 P.S. I'm also working on a (very secret) special project for the remainder of the year. I will share when the time's right or when I stop overthinking this announcement...whichever comes first.

Just got accepted to YC Startup School and I could not be more excited! 10 months ago, I had no clue what YC even meant. Now, it is the very platform that accounts for most of my growth in software, business, product, and the startup space as a whole. From working for a YC startup these past couple of months, I have learned firsthand the work systems and mindsets that are crucial to startup success. Now, I will have the opportunity to learn from some of the most successful minds in all of tech like Sam Altman and Jensen Huang , to build even more with $25,000 worth of AI credits 😁 , and to meet tons of like-minded peers at Startup School! I cannot wait for this opportunity! If you're going too, hmu I'd love to connect!

I had an incredible experience at the Kelley On Campus experience for my MBA at Indiana University - Kelley School of Business ! One of the highlights was competing in a business case competition alongside my team, where we were able to collaborate, problem-solve, and present our ideas after a lot of hard work throughout the week. Beyond the competition itself, what made this experience truly memorable was finally meeting so many classmates in person after spending months seeing each other over Zoom during class. It was amazing building real connections with people from all across the U.S., all coming from different industries, backgrounds, and career paths. Between networking events, conversations, and team collaboration, I walked away with not only new experiences and perspectives, but also many new close friendships and unforgettable memories. A huge thank you to the Kelley Direct Programs staff Will Geoghegan , Julia Ailes, Ed.D. , Blake Mathias , Miki Pike Hamstra , Abigail Gschwend , Courtney Daily , Lindsey Spoonmore and more for organizing such a well-run and meaningful experience. I’m grateful for all the effort that went into bringing everyone together and creating an environment that made learning, collaboration, and connection so enjoyable. #KelleyDirect #MBA #IndianaUniversity #Networking #Leadership #Teamwork

As the summer begins, I wanted to reflect on major milestones that have happened! I graduated with a Bachelor's of Science in Statistics and Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC)! This degree not only gave me a strong understanding of data modeling and mathematical statistics but also gave me the computational foundation to create full-stack applications. I am currently interning with Bayer in Boston again! My experience last year was unforgettable, and I am excited to keep expanding my knowledge of Bayer's many different functions. Thank you so much to Katie Nebel , Blake Giles , Prithvi Prakash , Andrew Branen , and Masha Trenhaile for your continuous support and guidance! Finally, I am happy to announce that I am starting my Master's in Computer Science ( Siebel School of Computing and Data Science ) at UIUC in the fall!! I am looking forward to build on my understanding of computer science and cannot wait to learn about more advanced topics. Along with this, I am excited to serve as your 2026-2027 Illinois Women in Computer Science President! So many amazing things have already happened, and I am looking forward to what's next!
